title: South Korea's National Security Office meets financial regulators on preventing secondary damage from hacking
date_note: Edaily gives 26 November as the meeting day; Money Today's article is dated 27 November and refers to the same day with 'that day'.
geo_basis: agency location, Seoul; the sources do not state a city
summary: Edaily and Money Today report that the National Security Office convened financial regulators and the Financial Security Institute to review how to prevent secondary damage from hacking. It asked financial institutions to strengthen two-factor authentication such as OTP, bring AI into fraud detection systems, and step up blocking and investigation of sites that illegally sell leaked data. Money Today quotes an official citing the recent KEPCO incident.
plain: South Korea's National Security Office met financial regulators and asked banks to strengthen two-factor authentication, use AI in fraud detection and act against sites selling leaked data.
exec: The National Security Office asked the financial sector to strengthen two-factor authentication, add AI to fraud detection and act against sites selling leaked data.
action: As the National Security Office asks, financial institutions should strengthen two-factor authentication such as OTP and bring AI into fraud detection systems.

validation.note: Edaily and Money Today (two publishers) both report the meeting and the requests; the office's press release itself was not read.
